bull_bear.body:
- Differentiated pure-vegetarian positioning - described as India's first / one of India's pioneering pure-vegetarian hotel and resort chains, and explicitly cited by management as 'a durable differentiator' in its competition mitigation
- Asset-light mix of owned, leased and managed properties, which management says 'collectively provide flexibility, reach, and resilience' and proved resilient through recent economic and geopolitical challenges
- Concentration in the affordable and mid-scale segment, the band most directly supported by the September 2025 GST reduction to 5% on rooms priced up to Rs 7,500 per day
- Predominantly domestic and leisure-oriented demand base described as relatively insulated from global travel volatility
- Pan-India footprint across 12 states and 22 cities, which management states helps mitigate geographic concentration risk
- Long-term operating leases of 10-20 years with a rent-free refurbishment window of three to six months, limiting upfront capital in adding properties
- Deliberate diversification into F&B, restaurants and events, a stream the Company says continues to grow faster than room revenue
- In-house revenue management system, Revyog, supporting pricing, inventory management and demand forecasting
- Legacy of more than 36 years in Indian travel and hospitality
- Low leverage - debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07 times, described as ensuring ample liquidity and financial flexibility
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Competition in the mid-market hospitality category — Management flags a competitive landscape marked by growing interest from major brands seeking to expand reach and depth in the sizeable mid-market category, alongside smaller individual players growing through word-of-mouth and new-age, tech-enabled platforms. Mitigation relies on brand strength, guest experience, compelling offers, expanding reach and the distinctive pure-vegetarian positioning as a durable differentiator.
- Unforeseen events denting travel demand — Socio-economic stability fuels both business and leisure travel demand; unexpected events such as pandemics, geopolitical instability and natural disasters can profoundly affect the hospitality industry. Mitigation is deliberate diversification towards F&B, restaurants and events alongside core hospitality, plus steadily improving service standards to support higher occupancy and average room rates.
- Seasonality and cyclicality of the business — The majority of travel is seasonal or cyclical, driven by weather and location-specific events, with revenues typically higher in the second half of the financial year - so a weak H2 or an adverse season disproportionately affects the year. Mitigation is year-round marketing and branding to sustain recall plus promotions aligned with seasonal trends.
- Business continuity risk at individual properties — Accidents such as fires, natural disasters and infrastructure failures could adversely affect operations. Mitigation is regular maintenance and upkeep of all properties, diligent adherence to safety regulations and periodic safety audits; management notes the pan-India presence helps mitigate geographic concentration risk.
- Geopolitical developments in West Asia and elevated input costs — The MD&A flags the ongoing West Asia conflict, global trade protectionism and tariff-related uncertainty, and elevated energy prices as risks to the outlook; near-term hospitality performance may be affected by West Asia developments and related aviation disruptions which could keep fuel, logistics and utility costs elevated.
- Loss of input tax credit under the reduced GST regime — Effective September 22, 2025 the GST rate on hotel rooms priced up to Rs 7,500 per day was reduced to 5% without input tax credit. The AR states the loss of input tax credit represents a trade-off for operators, even though the net effect is expected to enhance affordability and demand in the mid-scale and budget segments where the Company's inventory substantially sits.
- Weather dependence / El Nino — The MD&A lists the possible emergence of El Nino conditions among risks to the India outlook; combined with the statement that travel demand is driven by weather and location-specific events, adverse weather is a structural demand risk for a leisure- and hill-station-weighted portfolio.
- Single-activity concentration in hospitality — The Company's disclosed business is a single activity - Hotel Management & Operations - with revenue earned only from rooms and from F&B/events at those same properties, so there is no non-hospitality earnings stream to offset a sector-wide downturn in travel demand.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Byke Hospitality Limited operates hotels and resorts in India's mid-market segment, serving domestic leisure travellers, pilgrims, wedding and MICE customers and business travellers in metropolitan, Tier 1 and Tier 2 markets and established and emerging tourist destinations. It owns, manages and operates its portfolio through a combination of ownership, long-term lease (typically 10-20 year operating leases) and management contracts, refurbishing and rebranding acquired properties during a rent-free period of three to six months before ramping management, marketing and distribution. Revenue comes from room sales plus food & beverage (restaurants and bars) and events, with a defining commitment to a purely vegetarian dining experience across its restaurants and banquets.

outlook.body:
- Pan-India footprint expansion with emphasis on metropolitan cities, Tier 1 and Tier 2 markets and both established and emerging tourist destinations; Mumbai and Delhi remain anchor markets
- Combine urban and leisure properties to diversify the revenue base, improve asset utilisation and build a stronger national footprint
- Add properties through acquisition in metropolitan areas while delivering a consistent, recognisable hospitality experience adapted to local market characteristics
- Invest in technology - the in-house revenue management system Revyog is progressing steadily towards profitability
- Strengthen Revenue Management Systems to use data and market intelligence for pricing, inventory management and demand forecasting, in order to improve Average Room Rate (ARR), occupancy and overall revenue performance
- Evaluate additional amenities and revenue streams to mitigate seasonality and improve property-level performance
- Build a digital presence aimed at Millennials and Gen Z on three pillars: social media and content (Instagram, Facebook, YouTube), influencer and creator partnerships, and personalised guest experiences using data and analytics
- Implement a loyalty programme to reward the most valued guests and drive repeat business and brand advocacy
- Preserve and lean on the Pure Vegetarian positioning as the differentiating brand proposition for a pan-India hospitality brand
- Conserve resources and reinvest rather than pay dividends, funding new projects and upgradation of existing properties
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The Byke's stated strategic vision is to expand its footprint towards 100 hotels and resorts across the country by 2030, from a current portfolio of over 1,744 rooms across 35 properties spanning 12 states and 22 cities, held through a combination of ownership, long-term lease and management contracts. In line with that goal the Company says it made eight properties operational during the year and acquired three new properties that are on track to become operational in due course, with several further projects underway. Expansion is pursued on an asset-light model: properties are generally taken under long-term operating leases of 10-20 years, with refurbishment and rebranding completed during a rent-free period of three to six months before a push on management, marketing and distribution across room sales and F&B/event revenues. Geographically the push targets metropolitan cities, Tier 1 and Tier 2 markets and both established and emerging tourist destinations, with Mumbai and Delhi as anchor markets; the Company says it recently strengthened the footprint through new property acquisitions in metropolitan areas. Alongside property additions the Company is upgrading existing properties (cited as a reason for conserving resources and not paying a dividend) and investing in technology, with its in-house revenue management system Revyog progressing steadily towards profitability. NOTE: the AR is internally inconsistent on the property count - the MD&A Business Overview states 'over 1744 rooms across 35 properties' and the Hotel Management & Operations paragraph repeats 'a total of 35 properties', while the 'Our Presence' infographic states '1740+ rooms spread across 28 hotels and resorts' in one sentence and '35+' Hotels and Resorts in an adjacent tile. No rupee quantum of capital expenditure is disclosed anywhere in this bundle.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Indian tourism extended its multi-year upcycle in FY2025-26 on favourable demographics, rising employment and increased disposable incomes fuelling strong domestic demand
- Within services, 'Trade, Hotels, Transport, Communication and Broadcasting Services' - the segment most directly relevant to the Company - grew by around 10.1% in FY2025-26
- Infrastructure investment and enhanced regional connectivity (including RCS-UDAN tourism routes) unlocked new leisure and pilgrimage circuits aligned with the Company's destination mix
- Hotel industry fundamentals improved: national occupancy approximately 64% in 2025 (2024: 63.0%), ADR up around 8.5% to approximately Rs 8,624, RevPAR up around 8.7% to approximately Rs 5,522 (Horwath HTL)
- Measured supply additions - ICRA projects demand growth of 8-10% CAGR against supply growth of only 5-6% over FY2025-FY2028, a demand-supply imbalance expected to sustain occupancy and pricing including in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets where the Company has historically concentrated
- GST on hotel rooms priced up to Rs 7,500 per day cut to 5% (without input tax credit) effective September 22, 2025 - improves affordability and supports demand in mid-scale and budget segments, which is where the Company's room inventory substantially sits; loss of input tax credit is the trade-off
- Union Budget 2025-26 personal income tax revisions raising disposable incomes, a favourable backdrop for discretionary categories such as leisure travel and dining
- Domestic travel propelled by leisure tourism, weddings, festive gatherings, business functions and corporate travel; domestic tourist visits of approximately 4,132.8 million in CY2025 are the most relevant demand base for the predominantly domestic, leisure-led portfolio
- Management describes robust growth in volumes and rates across many of its brands with an increase in margins during FY 2025-26

risks.risk: Competition in the mid-market hospitality category
risks.note: Management flags a competitive landscape marked by growing interest from major brands seeking to expand reach and depth in the sizeable mid-market category, alongside smaller individual players growing through word-of-mouth and new-age, tech-enabled platforms. Mitigation relies on brand strength, guest experience, compelling offers, expanding reach and the distinctive pure-vegetarian positioning as a durable differentiator.

Socio-economic stability fuels both business and leisure travel demand; unexpected events such as pandemics, geopolitical instability and natural disasters can profoundly affect the hospitality industry. Mitigation is deliberate diversification towards F&B, restaurants and events alongside core hospitality, plus steadily improving service standards to support higher occupancy and average room rates.

risks.risk: Seasonality and cyclicality of the business
risks.note: The majority of travel is seasonal or cyclical, driven by weather and location-specific events, with revenues typically higher in the second half of the financial year - so a weak H2 or an adverse season disproportionately affects the year. Mitigation is year-round marketing and branding to sustain recall plus promotions aligned with seasonal trends.

risks.risk: Business continuity risk at individual properties
risks.note: Accidents such as fires, natural disasters and infrastructure failures could adversely affect operations. Mitigation is regular maintenance and upkeep of all properties, diligent adherence to safety regulations and periodic safety audits; management notes the pan-India presence helps mitigate geographic concentration risk.

risks.risk: Geopolitical developments in West Asia and elevated input costs
risks.note: The MD&A flags the ongoing West Asia conflict, global trade protectionism and tariff-related uncertainty, and elevated energy prices as risks to the outlook; near-term hospitality performance may be affected by West Asia developments and related aviation disruptions which could keep fuel, logistics and utility costs elevated.

risks.risk: Loss of input tax credit under the reduced GST regime
risks.note: Effective September 22, 2025 the GST rate on hotel rooms priced up to Rs 7,500 per day was reduced to 5% without input tax credit. The AR states the loss of input tax credit represents a trade-off for operators, even though the net effect is expected to enhance affordability and demand in the mid-scale and budget segments where the Company's inventory substantially sits.

The MD&A lists the possible emergence of El Nino conditions among risks to the India outlook; combined with the statement that travel demand is driven by weather and location-specific events, adverse weather is a structural demand risk for a leisure- and hill-station-weighted portfolio.

The Company's disclosed business is a single activity - Hotel Management & Operations - with revenue earned only from rooms and from F&B/events at those same properties, so there is no non-hospitality earnings stream to offset a sector-wide downturn in travel demand.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: The Byke Hospitality is a mid-market Indian hotel and resort chain that pioneered India's first pure-vegetarian chain of hotels and resorts, operating 35 properties across 12 states and 22 cities on an asset-light mix of owned, leased and managed assets.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Byke Hospitality Limited operates hotels and resorts in India's mid-market segment, serving domestic leisure travellers, pilgrims, wedding and MICE customers and business travellers in metropolitan, Tier 1 and Tier 2 markets and established and emerging tourist destinations. It owns, manages and operates its portfolio through a combination of ownership, long-term lease (typically 10-20 year operating leases) and management contracts, refurbishing and rebranding acquired properties during a rent-free period of three to six months before ramping management, marketing and distribution. Revenue comes from room sales plus food & beverage (restaurants and bars) and events, with a defining commitment to a purely vegetarian dining experience across its restaurants and banquets.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Hotel Management & Operations:** The Byke (rooms / hospitality), Food & beverage - restaurants and bars, Events and banqueting, Farm Fresh (restaurant brand), Revyog (in-house revenue management system)
- **Property formats:** Leisure resorts, Business hotels, Pilgrimage hotels, Boutique hotels, Service apartments

end_markets.title: End Markets (RHP)
end_markets.body:
- Domestic leisure travellers (predominantly domestic, leisure-led demand base)
- Mid-market / affordable and mid-scale segment travellers
- Pilgrimage and spiritual travel circuits
- Weddings, festive gatherings and MICE / banqueting customers
- Business travellers in metropolitan and Tier 1 markets
- India only - 12 states and 22 cities; Mumbai and Delhi as anchor markets
- Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets where the Company has historically concentrated its presence

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian tourism extended its multi-year upcycle in FY2025-26 on favourable demographics, rising employment and increased disposable incomes fuelling strong domestic demand
- Within services, 'Trade, Hotels, Transport, Communication and Broadcasting Services' - the segment most directly relevant to the Company - grew by around 10.1% in FY2025-26
- Infrastructure investment and enhanced regional connectivity (including RCS-UDAN tourism routes) unlocked new leisure and pilgrimage circuits aligned with the Company's destination mix
- Hotel industry fundamentals improved: national occupancy approximately 64% in 2025 (2024: 63.0%), ADR up around 8.5% to approximately Rs 8,624, RevPAR up around 8.7% to approximately Rs 5,522 (Horwath HTL)
- Measured supply additions - ICRA projects demand growth of 8-10% CAGR against supply growth of only 5-6% over FY2025-FY2028, a demand-supply imbalance expected to sustain occupancy and pricing including in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets where the Company has historically concentrated
- GST on hotel rooms priced up to Rs 7,500 per day cut to 5% (without input tax credit) effective September 22, 2025 - improves affordability and supports demand in mid-scale and budget segments, which is where the Company's room inventory substantially sits; loss of input tax credit is the trade-off
- Union Budget 2025-26 personal income tax revisions raising disposable incomes, a favourable backdrop for discretionary categories such as leisure travel and dining
- Domestic travel propelled by leisure tourism, weddings, festive gatherings, business functions and corporate travel; domestic tourist visits of approximately 4,132.8 million in CY2025 are the most relevant demand base for the predominantly domestic, leisure-led portfolio
- Management describes robust growth in volumes and rates across many of its brands with an increase in margins during FY 2025-26

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Pan-India footprint expansion with emphasis on metropolitan cities, Tier 1 and Tier 2 markets and both established and emerging tourist destinations; Mumbai and Delhi remain anchor markets
- Combine urban and leisure properties to diversify the revenue base, improve asset utilisation and build a stronger national footprint
- Add properties through acquisition in metropolitan areas while delivering a consistent, recognisable hospitality experience adapted to local market characteristics
- Invest in technology - the in-house revenue management system Revyog is progressing steadily towards profitability
- Strengthen Revenue Management Systems to use data and market intelligence for pricing, inventory management and demand forecasting, in order to improve Average Room Rate (ARR), occupancy and overall revenue performance
- Evaluate additional amenities and revenue streams to mitigate seasonality and improve property-level performance
- Build a digital presence aimed at Millennials and Gen Z on three pillars: social media and content (Instagram, Facebook, YouTube), influencer and creator partnerships, and personalised guest experiences using data and analytics
- Implement a loyalty programme to reward the most valued guests and drive repeat business and brand advocacy
- Preserve and lean on the Pure Vegetarian positioning as the differentiating brand proposition for a pan-India hospitality brand
- Conserve resources and reinvest rather than pay dividends, funding new projects and upgradation of existing properties

Geographically the push targets metropolitan cities, Tier 1 and Tier 2 markets and both established and emerging tourist destinations, with Mumbai and Delhi as anchor markets; the Company says it recently strengthened the footprint through new property acquisitions in metropolitan areas. Alongside property additions the Company is upgrading existing properties (cited as a reason for conserving resources and not paying a dividend) and investing in technology, with its in-house revenue management system Revyog progressing steadily towards profitability. moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Differentiated pure-vegetarian positioning - described as India's first / one of India's pioneering pure-vegetarian hotel and resort chains, and explicitly cited by management as 'a durable differentiator' in its competition mitigation
- Asset-light mix of owned, leased and managed properties, which management says 'collectively provide flexibility, reach, and resilience' and proved resilient through recent economic and geopolitical challenges
- Concentration in the affordable and mid-scale segment, the band most directly supported by the September 2025 GST reduction to 5% on rooms priced up to Rs 7,500 per day
- Predominantly domestic and leisure-oriented demand base described as relatively insulated from global travel volatility
- Pan-India footprint across 12 states and 22 cities, which management states helps mitigate geographic concentration risk
- Long-term operating leases of 10-20 years with a rent-free refurbishment window of three to six months, limiting upfront capital in adding properties
- Deliberate diversification into F&B, restaurants and events, a stream the Company says continues to grow faster than room revenue
- In-house revenue management system, Revyog, supporting pricing, inventory management and demand forecasting
- Legacy of more than 36 years in Indian travel and hospitality
- Low leverage - debt-to-equity ratio of 0.07 times, described as ensuring ample liquidity and financial flexibility

Mitigation is year-round marketing and branding to sustain recall plus promotions aligned with seasonal trends.
- Business continuity risk at individual properties — Accidents such as fires, natural disasters and infrastructure failures could adversely affect operations. The AR states the loss of input tax credit represents a trade-off for operators, even though the net effect is expected to enhance affordability and demand in the mid-scale and budget segments where the Company's inventory substantially sits.

- Single-activity concentration in hospitality — The Company's disclosed business is a single activity - Hotel Management & Operations - with revenue earned only from rooms and from F&B/events at those same properties, so there is no non-hospitality earnings stream to offset a sector-wide downturn in travel demand.
